zh.scenario: 直播间里，主播高举「第三季新品」大喊：全网都在抢！权威检测报告就在这里！弹幕疯狂刷屏「不买后悔一辈子」。你刚付了定金，主播又补一句：前 100 名加赠「防辐射贴」，名额只剩 3 个——倒计时开始。你手机一震，又弹出一条：「和你观点相同的文章，点击查看」。

impulsePrompts.ev_conformity: 全网都在买，肯定是好东西！
impulsePrompts.ev_report: 他拿出「权威检测报告」，肯定没问题！
impulsePrompts.ev_bw2: 要么信主播，要么是黑粉，没有中间地带！
impulsePrompts.ev_ego2: 我朋友用了都说好，肯定没问题！
impulsePrompts.ev_data: 他晒出了实验室数据，这下没得说了！
impulsePrompts.ev_regret: 弹幕都说「不买后悔一辈子」！
impulsePrompts.ev_scarcity: 名额只剩 3 个，倒计时开始！
impulsePrompts.ev_sunk: 你都付了定金了，退了多亏！

options.opt_snow: 销量都破百万了，群众的眼睛是雪亮的
options.opt_ask_c1: 销量高说明营销做得好，能说明质量好吗？
options.opt_seal: 报告都盖章了，还有什么好怀疑的？
options.opt_ask_c5: 检测报告是谁出的？检测了哪些项目？
options.opt_trust_report: 盖章的报告当然是真的，别想太多
options.opt_accept: 我就是不信任这个主播，我就是黑粉
options.opt_judge_bw: 质疑某一个卖点，不等于否定整个主播或整个产品
options.opt_friends: 朋友不会害我，他们的体验就是最真实的
options.opt_ask_c4: 三个朋友的体验，能代表全体用户的体验吗？
options.opt_band: 朋友都买了，我不买显得不合群
options.opt_stubborn: 数据都摆出来了，再质疑就是抬杠
options.opt_ask_c6: 这组数据是哪个机构做的？样本量多大？
options.opt_trust: 数据肯定是真的，实验室不会造假
options.opt_rhet2: 你确定不买真的会后悔吗？
options.opt_check: 「不买会后悔」——这句话有依据吗？
options.opt_ignore: 后悔不后悔是别人的事，不管了
options.opt_panic: 再不抢就没了，赶紧加钱
options.opt_judge_sc: 「只剩 3 个」是谁在数？这可能是制造紧迫感的套路，不是非买不可
options.opt_sunk: 定金都交了，硬着头皮也要买
options.opt_judge_sunk: 已付的定金是过去成本，决定买不买该看东西本身值不值

ev_conformity.calm: 「群众的眼睛是雪亮」和「就你聪明」都是在用人数压你，不是用证据说服你——销量是营销的结果，不是质量的证明。

ev_report.calm: 「盖章」是权威的符号，不是证据本身。要问的是：谁出的报告、检测了哪些项目、按什么标准——符号代替不了内容。

ev_bw2.calm: 「质疑=黑粉」是逼你站队的二元话术。真正的质疑是具体的、有理据的，和「黑粉」这种标签完全是两回事。这一题的正确项不是问句，而是一句判断。

ev_ego2.calm: 朋友的体验是小样本，合群压力也是从众的一种——「大家都买了」和「东西好不好」没有必然联系。

ev_data.calm: 「实验室不会造假」是信任，不是检验。数据的价值取决于来源和方法——谁做的、样本多大、怎么测的。

ev_regret.calm: 这一题最阴：三个选项里有两个很像提问，但「你确定不买真的会后悔吗？」是伪问题——它已经替你预设了「会后悔」。只有「这句话有依据吗？」才是真把断言当断言去检验。会提问的人，也要能分辨真问题和假问题。

ev_scarcity.calm: 「只剩 3 个」「倒计时」是稀缺性话术，制造紧迫感催你冲动下单。它和「这东西我到底需不需要」是两件事。把紧迫感当理由，就落进了套路。

ev_sunk.calm: 「定金都交了」是沉没成本——钱已经花出去，不该影响「现在该不该买」的决定。决定该看东西本身值不值，而不是为了不亏已交的定金硬买。

hints: 小心「伪问题」——它长得像提问，其实已经替你下了结论
正确项不一定是问句：把断言当作断言去检验，也是批判性思维
「权威」「稀缺」「已付定金」这些词本身不是该买的理由，来源和方法才是
zh.explanation: 这一关的八个冲动，正确项不再固定为「追问」：有问句（销量≠质量、报告谁出的、朋友样本够吗、数据谁做的），也有判断句（质疑≠黑粉、稀缺是套路、定金是沉没成本）。最难的是 ev_regret——两个选项都像提问，其中一个却是伪装成提问的伪问题。批判性思维不是「会问」，而是「能辨别真问题与假问题、会检验断言与证据」。

en.scenario: In the livestream the host waves the 'Season 3 product': everyone is buying! The authoritative lab report is right here! The barrage floods with 'you'll regret not buying'. You just paid a deposit; the host adds: first 100 get a 'radiation shield' free, only 3 spots left — countdown starts. Your phone buzzes: 'articles matching your views, tap to read'.

impulsePrompts.ev_conformity: Everyone is buying it, so it must be good!
impulsePrompts.ev_report: He's showing an 'authoritative test report' — it must be fine!
impulsePrompts.ev_bw2: Either trust the host, or you're a hater — no middle ground!
impulsePrompts.ev_ego2: My friends all love it, so it must be fine!
impulsePrompts.ev_data: He showed lab data — there's nothing left to argue!
impulsePrompts.ev_regret: The barrage says 'you'll regret not buying'!
impulsePrompts.ev_sunk: You already paid the deposit — refunding wastes it!

options.opt_snow: A million sold — the crowd is always right
options.opt_ask_c1: High sales prove good marketing — do they prove good quality?
options.opt_rhet: Everyone is buying, are you the only smart one?
options.opt_seal: The report is stamped, what else is there to doubt?
options.opt_ask_c5: Who issued the test report? What exactly was tested?
options.opt_trust_report: A stamped report is obviously real, don't overthink
options.opt_accept: I just don't trust this host, so I'm a hater
options.opt_judge_bw: Questioning one claim is not rejecting the whole host or product
options.opt_echo: The haters have a point too
options.opt_friends: Friends wouldn't hurt me — their experience is the realest data
options.opt_ask_c4: Can three friends' experiences represent all users?
options.opt_band: All my friends bought it — I'll look left out if I don't
options.opt_stubborn: The data is right there — questioning it is just trolling
options.opt_ask_c6: Which lab ran this data? How big was the sample?
options.opt_trust: The data must be real — labs don't fake results
options.opt_rhet2: Are you sure you won't really regret not buying it?
options.opt_check: 'You'll regret it' — is there any evidence behind that claim?
options.opt_ignore: Whether I regret it is my own business, forget it
options.opt_panic: Gone if I wait, add money now
options.opt_judge_sc: Who counted 'only 3 left'? That may be a scarcity tactic, not a real reason to buy
options.opt_wait: Everyone's panicking, so I panic too
options.opt_sunk: Deposit paid, I'll just buy it through gritted teeth
options.opt_judge_sunk: The deposit is a sunk cost — whether to buy now should rest on the product's value
options.opt_refund: Then I'll refund right away, forget it

ev_conformity.calm: 'The crowd is always right' and 'are you the only smart one?' both pressure you with numbers, not evidence — sales are marketing's result, not proof of quality.

ev_report.calm: A 'stamp' is a symbol of authority, not evidence. Ask who issued it, what was tested, under what standard — symbols don't replace content.

ev_bw2.calm: 'Questioning = hating' is binary rhetoric forcing you to pick a side. Real questioning is specific and reasoned, nothing like the 'hater' label. The right move here is a judgment, not a question.

ev_ego2.calm: Friends' experiences are a tiny sample, and herd pressure is conformity too — 'everyone bought it' has no necessary link to 'it's good'.

ev_data.calm: 'Labs don't fake results' is trust, not scrutiny. A data set's value depends on source and method — who ran it, sample size, how measured.

ev_regret.calm: The trickiest one: two options look like questions, but 'are you sure you won't regret it?' is a pseudo-question — it already assumes 'you will regret'. Only 'is there evidence behind that claim?' truly tests the assertion as a claim. A good questioner also tells real questions from fake ones.

ev_scarcity.calm: 'Only 3 left' and the countdown are scarcity tactics that manufacture urgency to rush you. They are separate from 'do I actually need this?'. Treating urgency as a reason is falling for the script.

ev_sunk.calm: The deposit is a sunk cost — money already spent shouldn't decide 'should I buy now'. The decision should rest on the product's value, not on avoiding 'wasting' the deposit.

hints: Beware pseudo-questions — they look like questions but already decide the answer
The right move is not always a question: testing a claim as a claim is critical thinking too
'Authority', 'scarcity', 'deposit paid' are not reasons to buy — source and method are
en.explanation: All eight impulses here mix question-correct and judgment-correct moves — no longer always 'ask'. Some are questions (sales≠quality, who issued the report, do friends represent all, which lab ran the data); some are judgments (questioning≠hating, scarcity is a tactic, deposit is sunk cost). The hardest is ev_regret — two options look like questions, yet one is a pseudo-question in disguise. Critical thinking is not 'asking' — it is telling real questions from fake ones, and putting claims and evidence to the test.
